sources.title: Endre Süli, Numerical Solution of PDEs, complete lecture notes
sources.locator: §3.2, PDF pp. 15–25: Lemmas 3–4 and Theorems 3–6 with their proofs; §4.1(a), PDF pp. 26–31: Lemmas 5–6 and Theorems 7–8 with their proofs.

contents.name: §3.2 Lemma 3 and Theorem 3: discrete summation by parts and uniqueness of the one-dimensional Dirichlet scheme
contents.reason: The source's telescoping identity is checked against the rectangular two-coordinate identity proved locally, including all four boundary flux terms.

contents.name: §3.2 Lemma 4: the discrete Poincare–Friedrichs inequality on a uniform interval grid
contents.reason: The source proves a one-dimensional constant independent of mesh width; the item derives the rectangular bound by a rowwise telescope.

contents.name: §3.2 Theorems 4–5: discrete stability and the C4 second-order error estimate
contents.reason: The source confirms the stability-plus-complete-residual route for the constant-coefficient case; the item proves the scalar variable-coefficient flux remainder locally.

contents.name: §3.2 Theorem 6: stability and consistency imply convergence for a linear elliptic boundary scheme
contents.reason: The local theorem instantiates the error identity with its own exact discrete inverse estimate and residual bound, without using the source result as a proof substitute.

contents.name: §4.1(a) Lemmas 5–6 and Theorems 7–8: two-dimensional summation by parts, discrete Poincare, stability and C4 convergence
contents.reason: These complete constant-coefficient proofs support the local grid-energy route; the authored theorem separately proves midpoint variable-coefficient consistency and exact-boundary error transfer.

reading_record.scope: The full reasoning for §3.2 and §4.1(a) over the locators above was inspected. The source's constant-coefficient and smooth-solution limits were retained; no variable-coefficient theorem was attributed to it.

sources.title: Benjamin Seibold, MIT 18.336 Lecture 5: Finite Difference Approximation
sources.locator: Complete seven-page PDF: pp. 1–4 Taylor stencil construction and multidimensional stencils; pp. 5–6 Poisson equations and Dirichlet/Neumann boundary rows; p. 7 course/legal page.

contents.name: Taylor expansion and coefficient matching for first- and second-derivative stencils
contents.reason: This supports the Taylor-residual method; the variable face-coefficient products and their explicit constants are expanded and bounded in the item.

contents.name: The one-sided Neumann approximation and its first-order boundary residual
contents.reason: The example computes the source's boundary residual exactly and solves the discrete error recurrence to verify that the global maximum error is h.

contents.name: The centered five-point Poisson stencil and its linear-system boundary rows
contents.reason: The example substitutes the exact quadratic samples into the five-point system and verifies uniqueness from the proved discrete energy lemma.

reading_record.scope: Every page of the seven-page lecture PDF was inspected. The first-order Neumann warning is preserved as a separate mixed-boundary example and is not included in the Dirichlet convergence theorem.

sources.title: Benjamin Seibold, MIT 18.336 Lecture 6: General Linear Second Order Equation
sources.locator: Complete five-page PDF: pp. 1–2 general and divergence-form variable-conductivity operators; pp. 3–4 residual identity, stability and error order; p. 5 course/legal page.

contents.name: Variable-conductivity flux form compared with the independently expanded differential operator
contents.reason: The example evaluates both midpoint flux and expanded centered formulas at a=1+x2 and u=x2, obtaining their exact h2/2 difference.

contents.name: Local truncation error, the global error identity, and uniform inverse stability
contents.reason: The lecture supplies the residual-transfer outline; the item independently proves the rectangular inverse estimate and the complete variable-coefficient residual bound.

reading_record.scope: Every page of the five-page lecture PDF was inspected. Its model problem and norm conventions are not generalized beyond the hypotheses and local proof written in this batch.
